\label{lesson:RU-C157-goluboy}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{голубой}}
\textbf{\ru{голубой}} (\emph{golubóy}) — \textquotedblleft{}light blue\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{голубой}} comes from \emph{\ru{голубь}}, \textquotedblleft{}a dove\textquotedblright{}, after the blue sheen of a dove's neck feathers (Vasmer).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{сладкий} (sládkiy)}{сладкий (sládkiy)}]{\ru{сладкий} (sládkiy) — sweet (taste)}

\label{lesson:RU-C157-sladkiy}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Russian for empty, then the Russian for light blue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{сладкий}}
\textbf{\ru{сладкий}} (\emph{sládkiy}) — \textquotedblleft{}sweet (taste)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{сладкий}} — taken from Church Slavonic, says Vasmer, in place of native \emph{\ru{солодкий}}: \emph{-\ru{ла}-} against \emph{-\ru{оло}-}. The native root is in \emph{\ru{солод}}, \textquotedblleft{}malt\textquotedblright{}, and Lithuanian \emph{saldùs}, \textquotedblleft{}sweet\textquotedblright{}, is a cousin.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Russian for empty, then the Russian for light blue, then say \emph{sládkiy} again

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{кислый}}
\textbf{\ru{кислый}} (\emph{kíslyy}) — \textquotedblleft{}sour\textquotedblright{}.

\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ru{вкусный} (vkúsnyy)}{вкусный (vkúsnyy)}]{\ru{вкусный} (vkúsnyy) — tasty}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ru{вкусный}}
\textbf{\ru{вкусный}} (\emph{vkúsnyy}) — \textquotedblleft{}tasty\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ru{вкусный}} is \emph{\ru{вкус}}, \textquotedblleft{}taste\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{-\ru{ный}}. \emph{\ru{вкус}} comes from \emph{\ru{кусить}}, \textquotedblleft{}to bite, to try\textquotedblright{}, which Vasmer relates to Gothic \emph{kausjan}, \textquotedblleft{}to taste\textquotedblright{}; its sense \textquotedblleft{}taste in art\textquotedblright{} copies French \emph{goût}.
\end{cousinweb}
